body:
## What I did

### Done

- Update all Vue, Angular, and Web Components snippets to have (if relevant) CSF Next versions
- Update _CSF Next_ API reference with new APIs
- Update _Writing stories in TypeScript_ guide with new APIs
- Audit and update prose for phrases like `default export` when referring to the "meta"

## Checklist for Contributors

### Testing

#### Manual testing

1. Sync this branch with locally running docs site
2. Check _all_ CSF-related snippets for Vue, Angular, and Web Components renderers

### Documentation

      [MIGRATION.MD](https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/blob/next/MIGRATION.md)

**Fix property access pattern in CSF Next example.**

The Angular CSF Next example incorrectly accesses `ButtonStories.Primary.args` directly. In CSF Next, stories defined with `meta.story()` expose their args via the `.input` property. This should be `ButtonStories.Primary.input.args` to match the CSF Next API and be consistent with all other CSF Next examples in this file (React, Vue, Web Components).



<details>
<summary>🐛 Proposed fix for property access</summary>

```diff
 export const Pair = meta.story({
   args: {
-    buttons: [{ ...ButtonStories.Primary.args }, { ...ButtonStories.Secondary.args }],
+    buttons: [{ ...ButtonStories.Primary.input.args }, { ...ButtonStories.Secondary.input.args }],
     orientation: 'horizontal',
   },
 });
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
In `@docs/_snippets/button-group-story.md` around lines 56 - 61, The Pair story
currently builds its buttons array by accessing ButtonStories.Primary.args and

story definition so the buttons array uses ButtonStories.Primary.input.args and
ButtonStories.Secondary.input.args instead (i.e., replace occurrences of .args
on those story references with .input.args inside the Pair story's

```
